biography: Buddy Arrington, hailing from the short tracks of rural Virginia, discovered his love for speed early. Tinkering with his father's old pickup truck, he honed his mechanical skills and a deep understanding of vehicle dynamics. His racing career began in local dirt track events, where his aggressive style and fearless overtaking maneuvers quickly gained him a reputation. A defining moment came at the '78 Backwoods 200, where, despite starting from the back of the grid due to a qualifying mishap, he clawed his way to victory, outmaneuvering seasoned veterans. Now racing for Stock USA Gen1, Buddy is proving himself a formidable competitor, blending raw talent with a calculating approach, aiming to claim a championship title.
drivingStyle: Buddy's driving style is a masterclass in controlled aggression. He's known for his late-braking maneuvers, diving into corners where others fear to tread. Tire management is a key aspect of his strategy; he conserves early in the race, patiently stalking his rivals, before unleashing his full pace in the closing laps. Under pressure, Buddy remains remarkably composed, making calculated decisions and rarely cracking under the strain. He has a knack for finding the grip where others can't, allowing him to carry momentum through the turns and maintain a relentless pace.

rivalries.reason: A bitter rivalry stemming from a controversial incident at the '79 Thunder Valley 300, where Jake accused Buddy of deliberately wrecking him in the final turn.
A clash of styles and personalities. Reggie, known for his flamboyant personality and aggressive on-track behavior, frequently clashes with Buddy's more stoic and calculating approach.
Rivals since their dirt track days, Cody and Buddy have a long history of close racing and occasional on-track altercations. Their battles are always intense and unpredictable.

quirks: Always wears a lucky horseshoe necklace given to him by his grandmother.
Listens to classic country music on his headphones right up until he puts on his helmet.
Has a habit of meticulously cleaning his driving gloves before each race, regardless of how clean they already are.
famousQuote: "Racing ain't about brute force; it's about knowing when to strike and how to sting."
careerHighlight: Winning the '79 Appalachian 500 after a strategic gamble on tires paid off, allowing him to overtake three cars in the final two laps.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the '78 Daytona 500 on the last lap while running in second place, costing him a potential victory.
